solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: As engine working with litter, this processes waste

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged, like parts of a running machine

explanation.surface: Some contraption combining an engine with rubbish is said to deal with refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges AS, ENGINE and LITTER, fourteen letters in all; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon, the lower bowel, is the organ that handles digestive waste before it leaves the body.

clue.text: See our way to change, that's unchanged

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the preceding words to be altered in order

explanation.surface: A plea to persuade someone to come round to our way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges SEE, OUR and WAY; the definition plays on the opposite idea, staying unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command to return to the previous position means things stay just as they were before.

clue.text: An expanding one right for surgery?

definitions.text: An expanding one right for surgery?

parts.words: An expanding one right for surgery?
parts.note: a waistline that keeps on growing might be a candidate for an operation such as a gastric band

explanation.surface: Something swelling is perhaps ripe for an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement round a person's middle is what grows with weight gain and prompts weight-loss surgery.

clue.text: Opening in mushroom, peculiar on it

parts.note: taken as written
a cep is an edible wild mushroom, the porcini

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of the following words are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange gap is found in some fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' signals the anagram of the last two words; 'Opening' at the front looks like a verb but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginning or start of something, an opening, is its inception.

clue.text: It's invigorating, note

definitions.meaning: something that refreshes or restores energy, like a medicinal drink
the first degree of a musical scale, its keynote

explanation.surface: A remark that something is refreshing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up drink is a restorative, and in music the keynote of a scale bears the same name.

clue.text: Male ego having change of heart, or cast out here?

parts.note: a stag is an adult male deer, and a stag party is an all-male one

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, and here that letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written before its middle letter is altered
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's vanity softens, or else the actors are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle G of EGO becomes D, giving EDO. 'cast' is not an anagram signal: it is the theatre cast, who leave by this exit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear entrance of a theatre is where the performers come out after the show.

clue.text: One held in reserve, not entirely Greek

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: not entirely means the phrase is cut short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: something put on ice is kept back for later use

explanation.surface: Someone kept on the bench is only partly Hellenic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final E of ON ICE, leaving ONIC after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic describes one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, and a dialect of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Glue ultimately odd coating animal, leaving fluff on paper

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word glue
coating means one piece wraps round another like a layer

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: Sticky stuff on a creature leaves fur on a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' is the container signal and 'leaving' only links. 'fluff' means a blunder, not fur, and 'odd' is the old sense of rum.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is a mistake in print, so a fluff or slip committed to paper.

clue.text: Son laughs at dresses

parts.note: to mock someone is to laugh at them

explanation.surface: A boy ridicules his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocks are loose dresses or overgarments, a type of frock.

clue.text: Dignitary uniting county and king

parts.note: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland
R, from Latin rex, abbreviates king

explanation.surface: A civic leader brings a region and its monarch together.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the ceremonial head of a town, a civic dignitary.

clue.text: Tin can or otherwise, finally, after recycling, tin can, say?

indicators.note: recycling turns material into something new, so these letters are reprocessed into another order
finally picks the last letter of the word otherwise

explanation.surface: A tin can or anything else goes into the recycling as a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link. 'finally' takes E from 'otherwise'; 'recycling' rearranges TINCANOR plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin can is one example of a receptacle, something that holds contents.

clue.text: I'm digusted having invested in great achievement — show me the money!

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into a venture, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant stroke or notable success
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone sickened after putting money into a triumph demands payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' is the container signal; the financial words in the surface hide it, and 'digusted' is the clue's own spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand over money reluctantly is to pay up, the demand of 'show me the money'.

clue.text: Redundancies made in naval style

definitions.meaning: cuts to a ship's company, its sailors laid off

explanation.surface: Job losses in the navy make a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short haircut is a style, and literally cutting a ship's sailors is a reduction in staff.

clue.text: Sound alloy for lift

indicators.note: sound at the start signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: steel is an alloy of iron and carbon

explanation.surface: A solid metal is used for raising something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for pinching it, to take without permission.

clue.text: Diver around western waters when no-one on the beach?

indicators.note: around means the bird's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: the loon is the North American name for the diver bird
seas are waters

explanation.surface: A bird swims round the western seas, an empty-beach time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' looks like a swimmer but is the bird, and 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-peak period for holidays is when beaches are deserted.

clue.text: Not out batsman's first casualty, second sent back — out!

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of batsman

parts.note: a casualty is a loss, as in war losses

indicators.note: sent back means the word for second is reversed

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the unbeaten batsman's opening loss, then another dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns MO into OM. The cricket surface hides the flowers: 'out' means blooming.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out are open and blooming, which is to say blossoming.

clue.text: Loop for fitting bits to old brogue, initially pulled up

indicators.note: pulled up reverses the whole run, since in a down answer up means upward reading

parts.note: bits are parts
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of brogue

explanation.surface: Pieces for an old shoe are hauled upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns the whole run PARTSTOOB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab at the back of a boot is a loop to help pull the footwear on.

clue.text: Composer's fine piece about machine, it's uplifting

definitions.note: the possessive reads as composer is, introducing the wordplay

indicators.note: about means the strip goes around the vehicle

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood
car is a machine

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word is read upward, that is backwards

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A composer's delicate work about a car is said to be inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'uplifting' turns the last piece upward in this down clue; 'fine piece' sounds musical but means a thin strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer known for keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Take trouble, having secured victory, to participate in sport

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of take are disturbed

parts.note: having secured victory is having won
to do a sport is to take part in it

explanation.surface: Go to some lengths after winning to compete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges TAKE into TAEK; 'Take trouble' looks like a phrase meaning make an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art practised as a sport.

clue.text: Washing machine secure in the end after spinning

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
after spinning means the result is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a butt is an end, as in a cigarette butt
to win something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A laundry appliance locks safely at the end of the spin cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after spinning' turns only the word for end, giving TTUB; 'in' is the container signal. Secure and win share the sense of obtaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is an old-style washing machine with separate washing and spin-drying drums.

clue.text: Have a go at traditional meal

definitions.meaning: a joint of meat cooked in the oven, the classic British Sunday lunch

explanation.surface: Take on a classic dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise harshly is to roast, and a roast dinner is a Sunday tradition in Britain.

clue.text: Nation's failure

definitions.meaning: a country, with the possessive read as is, linking
a flop, especially a show or film that bombs

explanation.surface: A country's flop.
explanation.definitionFit: The country between Europe and Asia shares its name with slang for a theatrical flop.

clue.text: Entrance painter with last of paintings

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of paintings

explanation.surface: An artist's arrival along with his final works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress means the act of going in, an entrance or way in.

clue.text: Politician perhaps, one of eighteen

definitions.meaning: a member of an environmentalist party
a putting surface on a golf course, which has eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A politician might be one in eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: An environmental party member is a politician, and a golf course has eighteen putting surfaces.

clue.text: Complainant claiming right — or more right?

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the litigant holds the letter

parts.note: one who sues is a suer, a complainant in law

explanation.surface: A plaintiff asserting his rights asks whether he is more correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claiming' puts R inside SUER. 'right' appears twice: the second is the definition in its comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Surer means more certain, which is more right in the sense of confident.

clue.text: Hollywood insecure (virtually) without religion

indicators.note: in puts LA inside the other word
virtually means almost, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened
Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Tinseltown is nearly insecure without faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insecure' splits into 'in' and 'secure'; SECUR (secure, 'virtually') takes LA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular means not concerned with religion, worldly rather than spiritual.

clue.text: Star starts to come earlier, lighting evenings brightly

indicators.note: starts to points at the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A star appears earlier, brightly lighting the evenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is informal shorthand for celebrity, a famous person or star.

clue.text: Person holding purse for all to see in wrongful rearrest

indicators.note: in places the certificate letter within the rearranged letters
wrongful suggests the letters of rearrest are set out wrongly

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A purse-holder appears publicly at a wrongful second arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongful' rearranges REARREST and 'in' puts U inside. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding the purse strings means controlling funds, the job of a club's finance officer.

clue.text: Turner in soap, to be concluded

indicators.note: to be concluded, like an unfinished serial, means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: lather is soapy froth

explanation.surface: A shop machine features in a TV soap whose episode ends on a cliffhanger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' is not the painter but a machine that turns wood; 'soap' and 'to be concluded' suggest a serial episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe turns a workpiece against a cutting tool, so it is literally a turning machine.

clue.text: In which sultana would never be queen!

definitions.text: In which sultana would never be queen!

parts.words: In which sultana would never be queen!
parts.note: a sultan's wife is a sultana, also a dried grape; in a state named after another fruit, a grape could never rule

explanation.surface: A country where a sultan's wife could never reign.
explanation.definitionFit: A politically unstable state dependent on one export, nicknamed after a tropical fruit.
